investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: WebSearch used solely as a discovery lead to find the candidate official domain; all retained evidence acquired via curl (raw HTTP, no WebFetch/AI-markdown conversion) against the site's public music-agenda list page and five detail pages, plus one contacts-page recheck. Inspected retained HTML for a source-defined event-type taxonomy, embedded schema.org JSON-LD Event/MusicEvent data, and a static price/admission DOM node. A dependency-free, no-network Node offline-proof script re-parsed the retained files deterministically to cross-check list-page event IDs against detail-page JSON-LD @id values and confirm field extraction. Level 1 was SUFFICIENT; no escalation to Level 2/3/4 was attempted.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET (BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 UA) of https://gulbenkian.pt/musica/agenda/ returned 200 OK with a fully server-rendered list of 24 event cards, each carrying a stable numeric data-event-id, a title, a source-defined event-type tag (fcg-card__meta-item: 'Concerto' on 22 cards, 'Transmissão' on 2), and a date/time text node. Following five of those cards' own hrefs to their detail pages (also plain curl GETs) returned 200 OK pages each containing a full schema.org JSON-LD MusicEvent/Event block with name, startDate, endDate, location, organizer, and a separate static DOM node giving price or free-admission text. The list page's data-event-id reproduced exactly as the numeric suffix of the corresponding detail page's own JSON-LD '@id' for all 5/5 sampled events (mechanically re-verified in evidence/offline-proof.mjs, no network). This already answers identity, platform classification, data-path discovery, and field assessment without needing to inspect JS bundles or open a browser, so escalation to Level 2 (STRUCTURAL) or beyond was not attempted.

venue_reference: Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian — Lisbon, Portugal (specifically its 'Gulbenkian Música' concert/agenda programme, one part of the foundation's much broader museum/gardens/orchestra/exhibitions/talks/film/education programme)

identity.notes: gulbenkian.pt was located via WebSearch as a DISCOVERY LEAD only, then independently re-confirmed by this investigation's own retained evidence: the retained list page's own <title> ('Agenda – Gulbenkian Música'), canonical URL (https://gulbenkian.pt/musica/agenda/), and page footer text give the foundation's real, well-known street address ('Av. de Berna, 45A, 1067-001 Lisboa'); every sampled detail page's JSON-LD names "organizer": {"name": "Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian"}. DISCREPANCY WITH AN OLDER, LOOSE NOTE: docs/LISBON_PORTO_VENUE_ESTATE_01.md §ranking notes a prior session's 'contacts-page fetch was blocked (403)' for Gulbenkian, treated in this repo's governance as a loose discovery lead at most. This investigation independently re-fetched https://gulbenkian.pt/contacte-nos/ just now (plain curl, same UA) and got a normal 200 OK with a full contacts page (retained as ev-contacts-page) — no 403 was observed on this specific music-agenda/contacts investigation, today. Current retained evidence wins per this task's instructions; the old note's finding may have been transient, path-specific to a different URL, or has simply changed since — it is recorded here honestly as a disagreement, not silently reconciled or assumed still valid.

site_classification.platform: WordPress multisite (site 3, path /musica/) serving a bespoke 'fcg-' prefixed events module (not a recognisable off-the-shelf calendar plugin such as The Events Calendar or EventOn) on top of a standard WP theme stack — evidenced by the wp-json REST discovery Link header, /wp-content/uploads/sites/3/... asset paths, and Alpine.js-driven filter UI on the list page. Each event's own detail page additionally emits a full schema.org JSON-LD Event/MusicEvent block, which is the most reliable structured field source.

data_paths.kind: WP_JSON_REST_ROOT (observed via Link header only, not explored)

title.notes: Reliably extractable from both the list page (h3.fcg-card__title) and each detail page's JSON-LD 'name'. Verified identical between list and detail for 5/5 sampled events (e.g. 'Vale do Silêncio', 'Oedipus Rex', 'Kafka-Fragmente', 'Quarteto Diotima', 'Beatrice Rana'). Left null here (a general capability finding across a 5-event sample, not one single event) — see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt for the per-event values.

start_date.notes: Each detail page's JSON-LD 'startDate' gives a full calendar date + time-of-day in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' form (e.g. '2026-09-05 21:30:00'), and the date portion cross-checks exactly against the list page's own human-readable date text (e.g. '05 set 2026'). This is a floating local datetime — no explicit UTC offset or IANA timezone is present anywhere in the retained HTML/JSON-LD; Europe/Lisbon is a reasonable real-world inference but was never promoted to a fabricated UTC instant. For a multi-session production (see 'end' below and Oedipus Rex in collector_assessment.blockers), the reliable per-occurrence date is the one on the matching subEvent[] entry, not necessarily the top-level MusicEvent's own startDate (which can span the whole run).

time.notes: The time-of-day portion of the same JSON-LD 'startDate' string (e.g. '21:30'). Same floating-local caveat as start_date: reliably extractable, but not a confirmed UTC instant since no timezone/offset is stated by the source.

end.notes: JSON-LD 'endDate' is present on every sampled detail page. For single-session events (Vale do Silêncio, Kafka-Fragmente, Quarteto Diotima, Beatrice Rana) the top-level endDate matches the single subEvent's endDate exactly. For a multi-session production, the top-level endDate instead spans the whole run (Oedipus Rex's top-level endDate is its SECOND performance's end time, not its first), while each individual performance's own end time lives on the matching subEvent[] entry. A collector must read subEvent[]-level dates per occurrence, not assume the top-level start/end always describes one single performance. Confirmed mechanically in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt.

venue_location.notes: Each detail page's JSON-LD 'location[].name' gives a Place name per event — usually 'Grande Auditório' (the foundation's main concert hall, at the foundation's own Av. de Berna, 45A, 1067-001 Lisboa address, itself confirmed from the site's own footer/contacts page), but at least one sampled event ('Vale do Silêncio') is an off-site outdoor concert at 'Parque Vale do Silêncio' — the source genuinely varies this per event rather than hard-coding one venue, and this investigation did not silently normalise the two into one address.

source_record_id.notes: The numeric id (e.g. 106594) is documented by the source itself as a canonical identifier (schema.org JSON-LD '@id': 'https://gulbenkian.pt/musica/MusicEvent/106594') and was proven empirically stable across an independent list-page rendering (its own data-event-id attribute) and the detail page's own JSON-LD, reproduced identically for 5/5 sampled events (evidence/offline-proof.mjs). This satisfies the stable-identifier rule (documented by the source AND proven empirically). IMPORTANT CAVEAT, documented honestly rather than smoothed over: this id identifies a PRODUCTION, not necessarily one single performance instance. A multi-date production (e.g. Oedipus Rex, id 106764, performed 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02) exposes exactly one top-level id shared by both dates; the individual dates live only in an unlabelled subEvent[] array with no id of their own. A future collector building per-occurrence Observation identity should NOT assume source_record_id alone is unique per date — the recommended alternative/supplementary identity strategy is a composite key of (source_record_id + subEvent[].startDate), analogous to how this repository already handles Hot Clube de Portugal's non-stable ICS UID per docs/OBSERVATION_PIPELINE.md.

event_url.notes: Each detail page's own <link rel="canonical"> and JSON-LD 'url' match the URL that was actually followed, and match the href on the corresponding list-page card. IMPORTANT CAVEAT, empirically discovered and honestly documented: a title-derived slug is NOT reliably reconstructable/guessable — this investigation initially guessed https://gulbenkian.pt/musica/agenda/beatrice-rana/ (no numeric suffix) and got a real 200 OK page, but it turned out to be a stale, unrelated 2020-03-24 Beatrice Rana concert (JSON-LD @id .../Event/65829), not the 2026-10-11 event actually listed on the current agenda (whose real, source-provided href is .../beatrice-rana-4/, JSON-LD @id .../MusicEvent/106821). A collector MUST take event_url directly from the list page's own <a href>, never construct/guess it from a title slug.

price.notes: Every sampled detail page has a static, server-rendered <dd class="fcg-event-ticket-price__value"> node giving either a price range (e.g. 'Oedipus Rex': '31,00 € – 70,00 €', 'Beatrice Rana': '24,00 € – 46,00 €') or a free-admission label ('Vale do Silêncio': 'Entrada Livre'; 'Kafka-Fragmente' and 'Quarteto Diotima': 'Entrada gratuita'). Recorded as a range/label string, never collapsed to one fabricated single number when a range was shown.

blockers.description: A multi-session production shares one top-level source_record_id/JSON-LD @id across all of its performance dates; the source exposes per-date subEvent[] entries but gives them no id of their own. A collector must synthesize a composite per-occurrence key (source_record_id + subEvent startDate) rather than treating source_record_id alone as a 1:1 event-instance key.

The source's own JSON-LD can disagree with itself about eventStatus: for the sampled Oedipus Rex production the top-level MusicEvent showed 'EventCancelled' while both of its own subEvent[] entries showed 'EventScheduled' (and the list page itself displayed a normal 'Bilhetes disponíveis' / tickets-available label for it). A collector should read eventStatus at the subEvent (per-occurrence) level, not trust the top-level field blindly, and should not silently pick whichever value looks more convenient.

Title-derived URL slugs are not safe to guess/construct — an older, unrelated historical event can occupy the un-suffixed slug for a recurring performer name (see field_assessment.event_url.notes). A collector must always take event_url from the source's own current list-page markup.

reasons: identity.status is PROVEN at HIGH confidence from this investigation's own retained evidence (page title, canonical URL, JSON-LD organizer, and the foundation's real footer address), independently re-established rather than assumed from any prior note.
site_classification.acquisition_class is JSON_LD_EVENT, a resolved/supported class — every sampled detail page carries a full schema.org MusicEvent/Event JSON-LD block.
Two data_paths entries (the list page and the detail-page pattern) are access:PUBLIC and status:CONFIRMED against retained evidence.
field_assessment.title.state and field_assessment.start_date.state are both PROVEN (start_date is not UNKNOWN/NOT_PRESENT).

field_assessment.source_record_id.state is PROVEN under the stable-identifier rule (self-documented by the source's own JSON-LD @id, and proven empirically stable across list-page and detail-page renderings for 5/5 sampled events), with an explicit, honestly-documented caveat/alternative composite-key strategy recorded in its notes for the multi-session-production edge case.
collector_assessment.recommended_family is JSON_LD, a known collector family, at HIGH confidence.

evidence/offline-proof.mjs + evidence/offline-proof-output.txt provide a DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION evidence item: a dependency-free, no-network re-parse of the retained fixtures that mechanically reproduces every field-extraction and id-matching claim above.

collector_assessment.blockers contains only MINOR entries (id granularity for multi-date productions, an eventStatus self-inconsistency in the source's own data, and unsafe slug-guessing) — none CRITICAL.

The source itself exposes an explicit event-type taxonomy (fcg-card__meta-item: 'Concerto' vs 'Transmissão') that was used to identify the music/concert sample rather than guessing from vibes; a future collector should filter on 'Concerto' (and re-review any other category values that appear over time) to keep to genuine live-music/gig programming and exclude broadcast/relay screenings and, more importantly, exclude this foundation's much larger non-music programme (exhibitions, talks, film, education), which was never in this investigation's retained sample.

This decision is a research conclusion only — it does not edit sources/*.json or any registry; turning it into an active collector is a separate, explicitly-authorised step per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md.
